reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
clinicalPearls: Results from defects in the biosynthesis of L-serine, most commonly 3-phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) deficiency, with allelic defects at PSAT1 and PSPH producing a similar spectrum
L-serine is a conditionally essential amino acid needed for phospholipids, nucleotides, glycine, and D-serine, so deficiency severely affects the developing nervous system
The classic infantile phenotype is congenital microcephaly, intractable seizures, and profound psychomotor retardation
The severe end of the spectrum is Neu-Laxova syndrome, a lethal condition with severe microcephaly, ichthyosis, and multiple congenital anomalies

The biochemical clue is low serine (and often low glycine) in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid, with CSF sampling being especially informative as levels may be low even when fasting plasma is borderline
This is one of the treatable causes of these features: oral L-serine supplementation, sometimes with glycine, can reduce seizures and improve outcome, especially if started early
Inheritance is autosomal recessive; prenatal or presymptomatic treatment is being explored for at-risk pregnancies
reference.pathophysiology: L-serine is synthesised de novo from the glycolytic intermediate 3-phosphoglycerate in three steps catalysed by 3-phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase, phosphoserine aminotransferase, and phosphoserine phosphatase. Because the blood-brain barrier limits serine entry, the brain depends heavily on local synthesis, so a block in this pathway causes a functional serine deficiency in the central nervous system. Serine is required for synthesis of glycine, D-serine (an NMDA-receptor co-agonist), phospholipids, and nucleotides essential for neuronal growth and myelination. Deficiency therefore impairs brain development, producing microcephaly, seizures, and severe neurological impairment, with the most profound defects causing the multisystem malformations of Neu-Laxova syndrome.
additionalDifferentials: Other genetic causes of congenital microcephaly with seizures
Glycine encephalopathy (non-ketotic hyperglycinaemia) at the other extreme of glycine metabolism
Ichthyosis-associated syndromes in the severe presentation
additionalInvestigations: Plasma amino acids showing low serine and often low glycine (fasting sample preferred)
Cerebrospinal fluid amino acids demonstrating low serine, which is more sensitive
Brain MRI for microcephaly and white-matter/myelination abnormalities
EEG to characterise the seizure disorder
Molecular analysis of PHGDH, PSAT1, and PSPH
Assessment of response to serine supplementation
redFlags: Intractable neonatal or infantile seizures with microcephaly requiring urgent evaluation
Progressive neurological deterioration in an untreated infant
Features of Neu-Laxova syndrome indicating a severe, often lethal phenotype
Missed opportunity for early treatable intervention
reference.prognosis: Untreated infantile disease causes severe neurological impairment, but early L-serine (with glycine) supplementation can markedly reduce seizures and improve development, making early recognition critical. The Neu-Laxova end of the spectrum is typically lethal.
pitfalls: Overlooking a treatable cause of microcephaly and seizures by not measuring serine
Relying on plasma alone when CSF serine is more revealing
Delaying serine supplementation, which reduces the chance of benefit
Not recognising Neu-Laxova syndrome as part of the same biosynthetic defect
references: Scriver's OMMBID: disorders of serine biosynthesis
Nyhan, Atlas of Inherited Metabolic Diseases
management: Correct the central serine deficit with oral L-serine supplementation, often combined with glycine, the definitive substrate-replacement therapy
Start treatment as early as possible, including antenatally in known families, because early intervention markedly improves neurological outcome
Control seizures with antiepileptic drugs alongside serine supplementation
Provide developmental therapies and feeding support for microcephaly and psychomotor impairment
Monitor plasma and cerebrospinal fluid serine and seizure control to titrate supplementation
Coordinate multidisciplinary care between metabolic medicine and neurology
Offer genetic counselling, prenatal testing, and family screening for this autosomal recessive PHGDH, PSAT1, or PSPH defect
